name: Romania
summary: The spouse, children and parents are guaranteed half of their intestate share. A foreign resident can choose the law of their nationality (EU Succession Regulation art. 22). Romania has a statutory fiducia in place of trusts; foundations are mainly for public interest.
reserved_share: Spouse, descendants and privileged ascendants (parents): half of their intestate share (Civil Code arts. 1086 ff). Gifts that infringe the reserved portion can be reduced at the request of forced heirs.
foreign_law_note: EU Succession Regulation: the law of the last habitual residence applies by default (art. 21), but a resident foreign national may choose the law of their nationality (art. 22).
trust_note: Romania is not in the HCCH table for the 1985 Trusts Convention. The Civil Code has a statutory 'fiducia' (a contract in which assets are held by a manager for a beneficiary), not a common-law trust; its articles were not confirmed. Foundations are governed by Government Ordinance 26/2000 and serve a general-interest or community purpose (not confirmed).
open_questions: Fiducia article numbers and OG 26/2000 purpose rules were not confirmed from the statutes.
Tax treatment of foreign trusts not sourced.

sources.title: HCCH status table: Convention of 1 July 1985 on the Law Applicable to Trusts and on their Recognition
sources.publisher: Hague Conference on Private International Law
